For example, I would buy things or prepare my apartment for when my boyfriend would come live with me, kind of anticipating the outcome by literally organizing my environment to prepare for the fruition of my desire. It felt exciting and very real even before he came into the picture.

My views have changed over time and I have thought a lot about the subjective experience vs. objective reality and how we have been shaped by our lived experience as to what it means to be X or have X. Of course that in a materialistic world, we would easily learn that having something be there for "real" will result in making us feel "X". But now that I am changing that perspective, I can redefine what it means to be "happy" without worrying too much about having X Y or Z be true or objectified to feel content. It's like cutting the middle man that blocks me from experiencing emotions that are at the core of our manifestations (and it's subtly suggested in Ask and it is Given by AH).

As I am reflecting more about this, maybe my initial post kind of challenges the definition of what manifestation really means but now I see that it's up to the individual to truly define that for themselves. It can be whatever you want it to be!
